title: The Minor road over the hill
subtitle: 决策选择 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）
meta: 主题语境：决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）　|　核心词汇：minor　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 minor 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1983 the nurse wrote of ① a minor road over the hill in the report, and everybody in the ward said at once that it was ② so minor that nobody in the ward would go near it. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the nurse, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the minor ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the minor road over the hill that anybody there had ever seen, or so the report for April 1977 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too minor to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the sufferer who had come to help; the minor ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the thermometer at the far cupboard, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a minor matter of detail, and said that no sufferer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as minor as the matter of detail they had once had in the old ward. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was minor or not, and he said so.

By 1990 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the report. What the line asked for was ⑦ something minor, and nothing besides. The sufferer from the next ward called the whole plan ⑧ quite minor; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the report kept the names of the minor ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1993, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another minor road over the hill in the same report, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ no less minor than anybody had expected. ⑩ The minor matter of detail that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1995, was the one she could never quite name; the minor ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 较小（前置定语 a minor road over the hill：1983 年护士在护理记录里记下的那件较小的小路）
B. adj. 较小／次要（两处加强说法：so minor that … 与 no less minor than …）
C. adj. 较小／次要（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 较小（表语 too minor to do：母亲觉得它太较小，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 次要（前置定语 a minor matter of detail：叔叔把整件事称作一桩次要的问题）
F. adj. 次要（同级比较 as minor as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩细节上的次要问题相比）
G. adj. 次要（后置定语 something minor：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 次要（受程度副词修饰 quite minor：那位病患的评价）

items.q: a minor road over the hill
the minor road over the hill that
The minor matter of detail that

answers.why: minor 意为“较小”，1983 年护士在护理记录里记下的是“一件较小的小路”，此处作前置定语 a minor road over the hill。
minor 意为“较小”，此处用 so minor that 结构，说它较小到病房里没人敢靠近。
minor 意为“较小”，护理记录上 四月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的较小翻山的小路，等于最高级的说法。
minor 意为“较小”，母亲认为这件东西“太较小了，谁也用不上”，too minor to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
minor 意为“次要”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩次要的问题”，此处作前置定语 a minor matter of detail。
minor 意为“次要”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩细节上的次要问题一样次要”，同级比较用 as minor as。
minor 意为“次要”，护理记录上那半行字要的是“次要的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something minor。
minor 意为“次要”，邻病房来的那位病患认为这套计划“相当次要”，quite 修饰原级 minor。
minor 意为“次要”，no less minor than 表示“其次要不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之次要不亚于任何人的预料。
minor 意为“次要”，母亲 1995 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的次要问题”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1983 年，护士在护理记录里记下了一件较小的小路。（a minor road over the hill）
它较小到病房里没有一个人敢靠近。（so minor that …）
母亲觉得它太较小，谁也用不上。（too minor to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩次要的问题。（a minor matter of detail）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩细节上的次要问题一样次要。（as minor as …）
到了 1990 年，护理记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件次要的东西。（something minor）
answers: In 1983 the nurse wrote of a minor road over the hill in the report.
It was so minor that nobody in the ward would go near it.
My mother thought it too minor to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a minor matter of detail.
He said nobody would call it as minor as the matter of detail they had once had.
By 1990 the report asked for nothing but something minor.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 minor 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1983 the nurse wrote of a minor road over the hill in the report, and nobody forgot it.
It was the minor road over the hill that anybody there had ever seen, or so the report says.
My mother thought it too minor to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a minor matter of detail, and nobody argued with him.
The sufferer from the next ward called the plan quite minor, and everybody laughed.
The minor ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
